events.label: Holmes's Handheld Stereoscope
events.description: Oliver Wendell Holmes designs a cheap simplified handheld stereoscope. The fork concerns whether he leaves the design open or patents and licenses it.

outcomes.label: Holmes leaves the design open
outcomes.description: Holmes deliberately leaves the simplified design unpatented, allowing inexpensive manufacture and rapid domestic adoption.
outcomes.rationale: The milestone's canonical description directly documents the open design and resulting mass adoption.
narrativeConsequences: Stereoview cards become familiar middle-class domestic media.
The medium establishes an early precedent for diffusion through openness rather than licensing.

outcomes.label: Holmes patents and licenses the design
outcomes.description: Holmes patents the simplified stereoscope and licenses it for a fee, prioritizing commercial return over rapid diffusion.
outcomes.requirement: Holmes or Joseph Bates decides the design's commercial value outweighs popular-science advocacy.
outcomes.rationale: Patent ownership is a direct effect; slower mass culture is modeled as reduced probability rather than an absolute prohibition.

influences.rationale: Licensing and higher prices delay broad adoption without making it impossible.

narrativeConsequences: Stereoscopic viewing remains an upper-middle-class practice for longer.
A licensing model becomes a visible precedent for later immersive-media ownership.

events.label: Stereoview Mass Culture Forms
events.description: Manufacturing, card publishing, and domestic adoption make stereoscopic viewing a normalized mass-market medium.

outcomes.label: Mass stereoview culture forms
outcomes.description: Stereoview production and circulation become broad enough to establish a durable domestic medium.
outcomes.requirement: Sufficient manufacturing and publishing capacity develops before the event window closes.
outcomes.rationale: This derived event makes delayed-but-still-possible adoption representable after either Holmes outcome.
narrativeConsequences: A shared visual vocabulary of travel, news, and domestic scenes develops around stereoview cards.

events.label: Lumière Cinématographe Exhibition Fork
events.description: Projected moving pictures become technically practical; the fork determines whether collective projection or Edison's private peephole model becomes commercially dominant.

outcomes.label: Collective theatrical projection prevails
outcomes.description: The Lumières secure paying audiences and cinema develops around projection to a shared public in darkened rooms.
outcomes.rationale: The collective exhibition model is the canonical historical outcome described by the milestone.
narrativeConsequences: Cinema becomes a shared public ritual rather than an individual cabinet experience.

outcomes.label: Private peephole exhibition prevails
outcomes.description: Patent enforcement or exhibition failure leaves the solitary coin-operated peephole model commercially dominant.
outcomes.requirement: Stronger Edison patent enforcement in Europe, or failure of the Lumières' Paris exhibition to draw paying crowds.
outcomes.rationale: The dominant social and venue forms are direct effects; the eventual cultural meaning remains narrative rather than hard state.
narrativeConsequences: Moving images develop socially like arcade cabinets or later headsets rather than theatrical cinema.
Any later collective cinema must emerge through a different event rather than being silently assumed.

events.label: Kinetoscope Parlors Become the Dominant Industry
events.description: Private coin-operated cabinets develop into the durable commercial system for moving-image exhibition.

outcomes.label: The parlor industry forms
outcomes.description: Investment and distribution consolidate around private cabinet venues.
outcomes.rationale: This event exists to make the Lumière counterfactual's immediate successor explicit and testable.
narrativeConsequences: Commercial moving-image culture standardizes around short, private, coin-operated encounters.

events.label: Shared Theatrical Cinema Consolidates
events.description: Projection, distribution, and purpose-built theaters consolidate collective cinema into a durable institution.

outcomes.label: The theater industry forms
outcomes.description: Shared projection becomes embedded in a durable theater and distribution system.
outcomes.rationale: This is a compact derived representation of the canonical collective-cinema lineage.
narrativeConsequences: Cinema architecture and distribution assume a shared audience as their default unit.

events.label: Sensorama Funding Fork
events.description: Morton Heilig completes a functioning multisensory cabinet combining stereo film, sound, vibration, wind, and smell; the fork determines whether any institution carries it beyond a prototype.

outcomes.label: No patron carries Sensorama forward
outcomes.description: Heilig fails to secure institutional or commercial backing, leaving Sensorama as an isolated prototype.
outcomes.rationale: Institutional failure despite a working prototype is the canonical milestone outcome.
narrativeConsequences: The somatic lineage survives as an idea without a durable organization or market.

outcomes.label: Private investors build a Sensorama arcade chain
outcomes.description: Private investors treat Sensorama as a premium amusement and fund a small network of commercial installations.
outcomes.requirement: An amusement or exhibition investor accepts the machine's maintenance costs and funds repeatable content production.
outcomes.rationale: Commercial backing is direct; eventual mass adoption remains unasserted.
narrativeConsequences: Somatic immersion develops through amusement economics and repeat customers rather than research procurement.

outcomes.label: DARPA funds somatic interface research
outcomes.description: Defense research funding adopts Sensorama's multisensory approach for simulation and training.
outcomes.requirement: A defense research sponsor treats wind, vibration, and smell as useful simulation channels rather than theatrical embellishments.
outcomes.rationale: The institutional home and research program are direct within the counterfactual; downstream consumer adoption is not encoded as certain.
narrativeConsequences: Somatic VR gains durable laboratories and procurement but develops under secrecy and training requirements.
Consumer uses may arrive later through technology transfer rather than direct entertainment investment.

events.label: Sensorama Arcade Network Forms
events.description: Commercial operators standardize Sensorama installations, maintenance, and repeatable content across multiple venues.

outcomes.label: The arcade network forms
outcomes.description: A small but durable commercial network establishes Sensorama as a repeatable paid experience.
outcomes.rationale: This is the direct successor implied by the authored arcade-chain alternative.
narrativeConsequences: Full-body sensory installations become a known commercial category rather than a single inventor's artifact.

events.label: Defense-Funded Somatic Interface Program
events.description: A durable research program develops multisensory simulation interfaces for training and mission rehearsal.

outcomes.label: The defense research program forms
outcomes.description: Funding, laboratories, and personnel establish multisensory interfaces as an ongoing defense research field.
outcomes.rationale: This is the immediate institutional consequence of the authored DARPA alternative, not a claim that consumer success follows.
narrativeConsequences: A generation of researchers treats bodily sensation as a technical simulation problem.
Somatic interfaces gain continuity at the cost of secrecy and limited civilian access.
